nm_lower_buttress_2.blurb: A small low block at the foot of the Overlook cliff in White Rock, near Los Alamos, at roughly 6,400 feet. It mixes short bolted lines with bouldering: four sport routes from an easy 5.6 up to a 5.10, plus six problems that are mostly V0 to V1 with a couple of harder ones, including a V5 on the boulder itself. The face looks east and gets morning sun that fades by early afternoon, which makes it pleasant on cool mornings. It is quick to reach and good for warming up, kids, or an hour of easy mileage before moving to the bigger walls above.

nm_big_pine_wall.blurb: A west-facing sport wall within the El Rito Sport Area in northern New Mexico, sitting around 7,600 feet. Ten bolted routes run from the upper 5.9s through the 5.10s and 5.11s, topping out with one 5.12. Expect cobble-studded conglomerate where the rounded stones and the pockets they leave behind serve as holds, on terrain that is slightly overhanging to vertical. It is a gentler, less steep cousin of the neighboring Rad Wall, with a couple of the best mid-grade lines in the whole canyon. Good for a climber working at 5.10 and 5.11 who wants sustained, pumpy movement.

nm_cuban.blurb: A single sandstone block in the Roadside Attraction zone of Mills Canyon, near Roy in northeastern New Mexico. It has four vertical to slabby faces with a flat landing at a friendly height, and ten problems that run from very easy V0 up to about V3, mostly at the low end. That makes it the natural place to loosen up before the harder boulders nearby, and a decent pick for newer boulderers. The stone is brittle, so it is a spot to save for dry conditions. A short walk up the hillside from the road, and the block can be spotted from the pullout.

nm_middle_rabbit_ear.blurb: The tallest of the three Rabbit Ears, a spire in the Organ Mountains above Las Cruces, at about 7,800 feet. Its climbs are mainly multi-pitch traditional lines of three to six pitches, from easy fifth-class up to 5.10, with two aid lines. The west face holds the best-known long route, a six-pitch 5.8. The north side has steep roofs for harder projects. Visits are quiet, so you are unlikely to share the wall, and you can time the day to climb in sun or in shade. The approach and the rappel descent off the south side are hot and tiring in summer.

nm_grandpa_smith_boulder.blurb: The biggest block in the Smith Family Boulders, a small cluster in the Pena Blanca part of the Organ Mountains near Las Cruces. Ten problems wrap around its west, south, north and east faces, with most falling between V0 and V3, one V1, and a single harder line at V5. The rock has interesting colors and varied faces, and the boulder makes a sensible warm-up before heading to the harder problems farther up the slope. It is the first group you reach from the parking area for the South Central boulders, and it is exposed to sun and wind.

nm_fire_tower_wall.blurb: A small crag tucked just below the lookout on the summit of Monjeau Peak, above Ruidoso, at nearly 9,600 feet. It has ten routes, mostly traditional with a pair of bolted lines, and nearly all of them sit between 5.8 and 5.10, with a handful of 5.10 minus lines. The wall takes a lot of sun, so cooler days suit it best, and the high elevation keeps summers comfortable. The cliff is hidden from view and reached by a short walk from the lookout, with bolted anchors at the top for rappelling in.
nm_fire_tower_wall.parking_note: Leave the car at the lookout near the top of the peak, which is the closest point to the crag.

nm_big_catch.blurb: At around 8,400 feet in the Jemez Mountains' Upper East Fork, this 100-foot bolted wall lies a short walk below the Spaghetti Western Wall. Ten bolted routes span 5.10 through 5.12, with a handful at each of the three grades. Most of the lines were put up between 2015 and 2022, so rock quality varies and some holds may be loose or dirty. Shade arrives from late morning on the right side and by early afternoon on the rest, while the grassy base stays sunny. The walk crosses the river repeatedly, wet in spring and dry later in the year.
